title: HSBC’s Head of Banking Says AI Deals Are Getting More Difficult
source_used: Bloomberg (text read via China Daily Hong Kong, which relays the Bloomberg interview)
key_facts: Michael Roberts, head of corporate and institutional banking at HSBC, said banks and investors are more selective and want higher returns to fund the AI rollout.
He spoke in a Bloomberg Television interview from Bangkok.
He said 'there's a healthy dose of skepticism' and that lenders will focus on proper returns and structure.
He said the deal sizes are very large, which makes them more difficult to do.
Global stocks are selling off after a plunge in chipmakers, and rising rates and multi-decade highs in global bond yields raise capital costs.
PwC estimates AI infrastructure spending could reach $8.2 trillion in Asia alone by 2050.
quote_evidence: I think there’s a healthy dose of skepticism,” Roberts said in an interview on Bloomberg Television from Bangkok.
“The deal sizes are very large, and by that nature, they’re more difficult to do.”
why_it_matters_hint: Lenders are asking for better terms on very large AI financing deals.
